parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by an ideal gas.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the temperature, in degrees Celsius, of absolute zero.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A sealed vessel contains a mass of 0.0424 kg of an ideal gas at 227 °C.
The pressure of the gas is 1.37 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume of the gas is 0.640 m³.

Calculate:
parts.text: the number of molecules of the gas in the vessel

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the mass of one molecule of the gas

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) speed *v* of the molecules of the gas.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The gas in (b) is now cooled gradually to absolute zero.

On Fig. 2.1, sketch the variation with thermodynamic temperature *T* of the r.m.s. speed of the molecules of the gas.

[[fig:f1]]

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A set of axes for sketching r.m.s. speed *v* against thermodynamic temperature *T* / K, with the axes marked at zero and the temperature axis also marked at 500.
